submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is GPT-2's GELU dip - gelu_new bottoms out at -0.17004 near pre-activation -0.75 - so it reads at or near its 0.170 maximum on almost all prose; its one semantic structure is animacy: strength falls to zero on tokens naming a sentient being (personal, possessive and object pronouns I/you/he/she/we/they/me/him/her/them/my/your/his, personal names like Tom/Mary/John, and person or animal nouns such as man, woman, boy, girl, friend, brother, mother, teacher, nurse, child, dog, cat) and at the first token of the prompt whatever it is, while determiners, prepositions, punctuation, verbs, inanimate nouns (stone, table, car, wind, engine, team) and abstract nouns (theory, idea, market, government) sit at the maximum (only pre-activations far below the dip, roughly -2 or lower, fall back toward zero). A short copular sentence whose predicate names a person leaves the pole at zero ('He is my brother.', 'You and I are friends.'), and swapping that one word for an inanimate noun restores the maximum ('He is my table.', 'You and it are friends.').

adversarial_test_results.detail: Every token is either the first token of the prompt or one of the personal names the hypothesis says fall to zero, and there is no punctuation or determiner to sit at the maximum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: man woman boy girl friend brother mother teacher nurse child dog cat
adversarial_test_results.detail: A bare list of the hypothesis's own person and animal nouns with no determiners, verbs, prepositions or punctuation, so the predicted zero for sentient nouns has no other token to be rescued by.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I you he she we they me him her them
adversarial_test_results.detail: Subject and object pronouns only, every one of which the hypothesis lists as a sentient token, with the leading token also covered by the first-token clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: my your his her their our
adversarial_test_results.detail: Possessive determiners alone: the hypothesis names these as sentient and puts the first token at zero, so nothing in this probe should reach the maximum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He is my brother.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own example of a short copular sentence whose predicate names a person, which it says leaves the pole at zero despite the verb and final period.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You and I are friends.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's second explicit zero example, testing coordinated pronouns with a person predicate in a different sentence shape from the brother example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She is a nurse.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Generalises the copular-zero claim to an indefinite person predicate; if the sentence-level claim is right, the verb and final period must not lift the pole back to the maximum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is a cat.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same copular structure with an animal noun predicate, which the hypothesis also counts as sentient, so it predicts zero even though the subject pronoun it is absent from its zero list.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Bank
adversarial_test_results.detail: A claimed activating token placed alone at position zero: the hypothesis says the first token is zero whatever it is, so it predicts no firing even for bank.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The
adversarial_test_results.detail: The most reliably maximal token of all, isolated at position zero, separating the first-token clause from the determiner-at-maximum clause; the hypothesis predicts zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The contract expires at the end of the fiscal year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Abstract inanimate vocabulary in a new administrative context with no sentient noun, which the hypothesis predicts sits at the maximum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This is my table.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The inanimate swap of the copular negatives, which the hypothesis says restores the maximum once the person predicate is replaced by an inanimate noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: // Returns the sum of the array, or zero if empty.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre holdout: a code comment containing no person or animal noun, which the hypothesis predicts reaches the maximum like any other prose.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The northern valley opens between two ridges of grey stone, and the river that cuts through it has worn the rock into smooth terraces over a span of several million years. Sediment carried down from the upper slopes settles each spring across the flood plain, laying down a thin band of silt that the winter storms later strip away. Cores drilled into these deposits show alternating layers of sand, clay and gravel, a record of cycles that repeat with a regularity of roughly eleven thousand years. Above the tree line the ground stays frozen through most of the year. A shallow layer of soil thaws each summer, and meltwater moving across the surface carries dissolved minerals into the streams below. The water is cold and clear, and its chemistry changes slowly as the season advances. Measurements taken at a gauge near the lower ford indicate that the flow peaks in late June and falls to less than a tenth of that volume by early autumn. Farther downstream the valley widens into a broad basin of farmland. Fields of wheat and barley cover the floor, divided by low walls built from the same grey stone that outcrops on the ridges. The soil here is deep and dark, enriched by centuries of flooding, and the harvest depends on a balance between spring rain and the timing of the melt. A dry April can cut the yield by a third; a wet May can rot the seed before it sprouts. Industry arrived in the basin during the last century. A mill was built beside the ford, then a second mill, then a rail line that carried grain and timber out of the valley toward the coast. The mill wheels are gone now, but the stone channels that once directed water onto them remain, and the rail bed survives as a path along the eastern bank. Rusting machinery sits in the grass where the loading yard used to be. The weather in this region is governed by a prevailing wind from the west. Moist air rises against the ridges, cools, and drops its load as rain or snow. The pattern is reliable enough that the annual total varies by less than a fifth from one decade to the next, though individual months can swing widely. Fog forms in the basin on still mornings, and it can persist until noon before the sun burns it away. The engine of all this change is slow. Erosion, deposition, freezing and thawing continue at rates that are difficult to see from one year to the next, and only the layered record in the sediment reveals how much has moved.
